findings.title: Scope of Work and Deliverables Defined
findings.rationale: The evidence clearly outlines the scope of work and deliverables under the agreement, detailing various products, services, and components involved in the BFSI deployments.
evidence_excerpts: The scope of this Agreement is intentionally broad, covering every category of hardware, firmware, software-adjacent service, engineering activity, logistical operation, and maintenance initiative likely to arise throughout the lifecycle of BFSI deployments.

findings.title: Service Level and Performance Commitments
findings.rationale: The evidence outlines the Vendor's commitments regarding pricing stability, service delivery, and the prohibition of unexpected charges, which are critical components of service level agreements.
evidence_excerpts: The Client shall not be obligated to pay for resource wait times, idle engineer hours, or vendor-driven deployment delays. This protects the Client from unexpected financial exposure and ensures absolute commercial predictability throughout the contract term.

findings.title: Client-Side Obligations for Vendor Performance
findings.rationale: The evidence specifies that the Vendor's performance is contingent upon the Client's requirements for manpower and operational dependencies, particularly for complex operations and installation services.
evidence_excerpts: If the Client requires manpower for complex operations such as security sandbox testing, PSU audit compliance support, mass firmware rollout campaigns, or large-scale device refresh cycles, such activities shall also be covered under the pricing model established in this Agreement.

findings.title: Performance Reporting in AMC
findings.rationale: The evidence specifies that the Vendor agrees to provide performance analytics reporting as part of the Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC), which is a key aspect of service performance measurement and reporting.
evidence_excerpts: Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC) shall also be priced under this Agreement, ensuring that AMC charges reflect industry-aligned maintenance obligations such as scheduled preventive visits, firmware patch cycles, device uptime monitoring, remote diagnostics, onsite support availability, real-time support desk access, and performance analytics reporting.
